items.summary: Research and educational instrument. Not for clinical use, for the care of any patient, or to determine or influence any drug dose. A simulation-calibrated informatics pipeline that fits a single-compartment exponential approximation to published population pharmacokinetic models of unfractionated heparin during cardiopulmonary bypass, and renders the result as an institution-specific decay nomogram. This is the supporting code and archived analysis for manuscript JCVA-D-26-01511. Published models of heparin disposition are biexponential and require a computer to evaluate. The pipeline asks how well a single decay constant k — calibrated to an institution's own dosing, weight and bypass-time distributions — can approximate a chosen reference model, and quantifies where it fails. The answer differs sharply by model: at the reversal timepoint the approximation holds to 0.38% mean absolute error for Lanoiselée and 0.44% for Jia, but to 10.3% for Delavenne, rising to 72% after repeated supplemental boluses. Contents. Five reference-model implementations with their published parameters and provenance; seeded cohort sampling and calibration; agreement statistics; nomogram geometry and rendering; a Streamlit dashboard; an automated test suite; and a frozen analysis run comprising 20 result tables, the main-text and supplementary figures, a run manifest and a manuscript-ready summary. A sixth model (PRODOSE-2) is implemented and tested but withheld from the active pipeline pending validation and peer review. Reproduction. Every reported number regenerates from one seeded command: pip install -r requirements-frozen.txt python run_analysis.py --seed 20260912 --outdir /tmp/check python check_frozen.py /tmp/check All randomness comes from explicitly seeded generators, each analysis stage drawing from its own independent stream. Re-running reproduces every archived result to within floating-point rounding on any machine, and byte-for-byte on the machine the archive was built on. The manifest records the seed, the commit, the package versions and every analysis decision. Continuous integration runs the suite on two Python versions, each test file again in isolation, and the reproduction check on every push. Verification, and its limits. Automated checks confirm that each closed-form solution actually solves its own differential equations and satisfies the identities they imply, and six landmark values from a published simulation are reproduced to within 3%. No participant-level data from any source study is held, so no model is re-fitted and no prediction is compared with an observation. What is demonstrated is faithful implementation of the published models — not that the published models are correct. No external or predictive validation is claimed. Scope. The pipeline represents the pharmacokinetic central-compartment amount only. It does not model the pharmacodynamic layer — anti-factor Xa activity or activated clotting time — nor peripheral-compartment heparin, antithrombin, protamine pharmacology or heparin rebound. Converting a residual amount into a protamine dose requires an institutional ratio that this software does not supply. Intended purpose. This software is a research and educational instrument whose purpose is to demonstrate and teach an informatics method under simulated conditions. Within that intended purpose it is not a medical device. Nothing here has been cleared, approved or evaluated by any regulatory authority; outputs have not been validated against measured anti-factor Xa activity, activated clotting time or clinical reversal in patients, and no clinical benefit has been demonstrated. Anyone using it outside the intended purpose does so on their own responsibility and may bring the tool within medical-device oversight in their jurisdiction; the authors accept no responsibility for such use. items.summary: Code and data supporting the article "Capillary-driven networks obey Murray's law everywhere except at the meniscus". The archive contains three things. A self-contained MATLAB package that builds the figures of the article and recomputes every number quoted in its text, using a backtracking Newton iteration on a scale-invariant objective and requiring no toolboxes. A Python module that carries the same model on arbitrary graphs, including graphs with loops, where the flow is obtained from the nodal Laplacian rather than from the topology, together with a script that runs the verifications of Appendices C, F and H: the nine-channel graph with four independent loops, the envelope identity, the sweep over the driving degree, the three terminal conditions, the power-to-cost ratios and the Kamiya-Togawa law, and the case of several dissipation mechanisms in one channel. And a pixel-level digitisation of Fig. 7 of Zhang and Lorente, Sci. Rep. 13, 11278 (2023), against which Sec. V of the article is compared, with the source raster, the recovered coordinates in three formats, and an image comparing the reconstruction against the original. Neither optimiser uses the sizing law under test: each maximises the throughput at fixed cost from the resistance and the cost directly, so the residuals reported are an independent check of Eq. (7) rather than a restatement of it. The digitiser is deterministic and reproduces its 298 recovered points byte for byte. Code is released under the MIT licence (LICENSE-CODE.txt); data and figures under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA.txt). The source raster in data/ is reproduced unaltered from a CC BY 4.0 third-party article and remains copyright of its authors; see THIRD-PARTY.txt. README.txt describes the contents, how to run everything, and which printed quantities depend on the configuration block.

items.summary: A three-signal stopping rule for iterative LLM refinement derived from the Möbius theory stack: an equilibrium-distance surrogate d̂_R (RZGM meaning-equilibrium layer), an update-free-recurrence and diversity-collapse detector pair (Reflective Homeostasis Layer), and a hard reflection-depth cap (MUSE bounded reflection). Pre-registered study: 500 English prose-refinement tasks across ten domains, two generator models (Gemma4 12B-IT-QAT and 26B-A4B-IT-QAT), 8,000 generations, 999 blind position-swapped pairwise judgments. The governor cuts refinement tokens by 36.6% / 33.1% (bootstrap 95% CIs 33.6-39.5% / 30.3-35.9%) versus an always-eight-iterations baseline — 2.2-3.4x a naive convergence stop — at a measured quality cost reported at equal prominence: 38.0% / 36.6% of judged comparisons lost overall, a majority among actual interventions (61.1% / 59.0%), with measured cost almost perfectly collinear with output length. A full-data ablation shows the saturation signal is simultaneously the savings engine and the dominant cost source, yielding a measured two-point dial (10.0-11.5% savings at 8.2-11.8% loss rate with saturation disabled). Pre-release adversarial verification (four independent refuter passes) confirmed all headline statistics against the raw data and caught an inverted flagship anecdote: the corpus's two catastrophic degenerations (~50 verbatim paragraph repetitions) were selected once and avoided once by the governor, undetected in both cases — set-based trigram signals are structurally blind to within-output verbatim repetition. All tasks, rollouts, verdicts, audit votes, and analysis code are released in the companion repository. items.summary: We present an HTTP threat detection system embedded in a production reverse proxy that achieves sub-500ns per-request inference latency. The system combines a depth-limited CART decision tree with a compact two-layer MLP in an ensemble architecture, where the tree provides fast-path classification and the MLP refines uncertain cases. Model weights are exported as Rust `const` arrays, enabling zero-allocation deployment with no runtime deserialization. We formalize structural safety properties of the ensemble in the Lean~4 theorem prover, establishing a three-tier verification approach covering structural invariants, weight-dependent decision bounds, and floating-point error propagation. In initial small-scale trials on a combined dataset of production logs, CSIC-2010, and CIC-IDS2017-derived features, the ensemble achieves >99% validation accuracy for both scanner and DDoS detection, with tree inference completing in under 2ns and full ensemble inference under 6ns. We discuss limitations of the current training data and outline directions for scaling to larger, human-labeled corpora.
items.title: Sub-Microsecond HTTP Threat Detection with Decision Tree–MLP Ensembles and Lean 4 Verification

items.summary: This work studies how small perturbations of the Enchan local time-rate field propagate through fine spatial structure in the same field. The problem is motivated by the hard-wall boundary used in a previous Enchan two-route interference study: rather than imposing a primitive material opacity or an S=0 wall, the present work asks whether finite structure in the Enchan field itself can generate scale-selective transmission and reflection. Starting from the reduced finite-tension branch S_tt = div[mu(D) grad S] - S with mu(D) = 1/(1 + D^(3/2)), the field is decomposed as a structured background plus a small propagating perturbation. Stage A uses a predeclared one-dimensional frozen structured background and compares it with a matched smooth/homogenized control. The response is banded rather than a monotonic low-pass: long-scale perturbations remain comparatively transmissive while strong reflection bands appear when the perturbation resolves the fine structure. At ka = 2 the mean Stage-A structured transmission is approximately 6.25e-4 while the smooth control remains approximately 0.989; at ka = 4 the structured transmission is approximately 1.07e-14 while the smooth control remains approximately 0.962. Stage B replaces the hand-constructed surrogate with three previously frozen source-free Enchan final states from the published localized-field study. The source files are SHA-256 checked against the original run manifest before analysis. All three source profiles remain within the declared positive longitudinal branch and reproduce a scale-dependent structured-versus-smooth transmission difference. The largest Stage-B mean differences occur near ka = 1.0 and 1.5, where structured transmission is approximately 0.330 and 0.358 while the smooth controls remain approximately 0.994 and 0.988. The maximum Stage-B conservation residual is approximately 1.89e-15. Stage C extends the test to a full three-dimensional propagation study using the same three previously frozen source-free Enchan field configurations. A total of 54 cases were evaluated across structured, smooth, and vacuum controls, three selected spatial scales, and both normal and 30° oblique incidence. The scale-dependent scattering observed in the one-dimensional diagnostics persists in three dimensions. Structured backgrounds show reduced forward transmission together with increased reflection and lateral scattering relative to the matched controls. At ka = 4 under normal incidence, the mean structured transmission is approximately 0.486, compared with approximately 0.527 for the smooth control and 0.532 for vacuum. The maximum three-dimensional energy-accounting residual remains below 1.2% across all 54 cases. The result supports a model-level statement: fine S-field structure can act as a wavelength-selective barrier for small time-rate perturbations within the declared linearized Enchan branch. It does not identify ordinary matter with the tested surrogate or source-free structures, does not claim monotonic high-frequency blocking, and does not claim that a macroscopic material wall has been reconstructed. The Zenodo deposit contains the Version 1.1 manuscript PDF together with the complete reproducibility package for Stages A, B, and C, including the frozen numerical code, Stage-C configuration, archived source states, full numerical results, summary tables, execution manifest, README, LICENSE, and SHA-256 integrity records. The manuscript PDF is generated directly from the final Version 1.1 TeX source and is set as the default Zenodo preview. Version 1.1 update: Version 1.1 adds the completed Stage-C three-dimensional validation, updates the manuscript and reproducibility package accordingly, and preserves the Stage-A and Stage-B results unchanged. items.summary: MATLAB implementation, per-item numeric results and figure code for the study "Dissociating Prompt Quality from Response Compliance in Automated Prompt-Engineering Assessment". A four-agent evaluator running on a locally hosted Qwen 2.5-7B-Instruct judge scores each prompt as an artifact before any response exists, then scores the resulting response twice on identical items: once against criteria extracted from that prompt, and once against a fixed rubric that never sees it. Verifiable constraints are checked with the IFEval reference implementation rather than model-generated labels. The whole pipeline runs on consumer CPU hardware with no external API calls. Contents: src/ the MATLAB agents and run scripts; scripts/ the IFEval verifier and the figure code; data/ a SHA-256 manifest of all 4,275 benchmark prompts and the filtered IFEval subset; results/ per-item results for the main run (n = 500) and the ablation (n = 120), the construct-validation output and the IFEval verification output. Corpus not redistributed. No prompt or response text from LMSYS-Chat-1M or WildChat-1M is included; the LMSYS agreement prohibits transfer to third parties and WildChat-1M carries flow-down obligations under the AI2 ImpACT licence. Prompts appear only as SHA-256 hashes, so an independently rebuilt corpus can be verified as identical to the one used here. The IFEval subset is included in full under Apache-2.0.

items.summary: Abstract Modern enterprise AI systems increasingly operate across multiple authorized data sources, memories, applications, and tools. This creates a security problem that is not adequately described as conventional data theft. An AI workload may be individually authorized to read support records, engineering information, source-control activity, supplier data, budgets, hiring information, and calendars. No individual source may contain a sensitive strategic conclusion. However, the AI system may combine those independently authorized fragments and reconstruct a new high-value object: an unreleased product direction, likely launch window, supplier dependency, market strategy, organizational weakness, or other forward-looking enterprise knowledge. The security boundary therefore changes. The relevant questions are no longer only: Who may read data A? or: Who may read data B? They also become: Who may establish the relationship A-to-B? Who may retain or disclose the resulting inference? Who may cause an external action because of that reconstructed meaning? This paper describes a threat model in which the AI assistant becomes a computational graph across previously separate enterprise systems. The resulting risk may exist even when each underlying retrieval complies with its ordinary source-level permissions. The sensitive object is not necessarily a stolen database record; it may be a new semantic object created through authorized association. The architecture therefore separates two security transitions: Authorized Data | v Authorized Reconstruction | v Computed Meaning | v Authorized Effectuation | v External Consequence The first transition concerns association authority : permission to read independently authorized fragments does not automatically imply permission to join those fragments into a new semantic relationship. The second concerns execution-time finality : permission to compute, generate, or prepare an output does not automatically imply permission for that output to become externally consequential. The proposed architectural model therefore introduces controls around independently governed relationship mapping, session-bound reconstruction, minimum-necessary temporary views, provenance-aware release, and a mandatory effectuation boundary. Candidate outputs or actions remain non-effective until the consequence-controlling component verifies the applicable authority, provenance, destination, policy state, disclosure conditions, and other protected execution state immediately before release or effectuation. In compact form: Access != Association Association != Authority to Disclose Computation != Authority to Cause Consequence The execution-time consequence boundary may be implemented through existing mechanisms such as policy-enforcement points, reference monitors, authorization servers, secure execution environments, transaction coordinators, capability systems, protected dispatchers, database commit controls, network command gates, or equivalent mechanisms. The important property is functional rather than terminological: A computed result or proposed action remains non-effective until the component with mandatory control over the actual consequence verifies that the exact pending effect is permitted under current protected authority and state. This architecture is intended to complement conventional identity, access control, encryption, zero-trust, data-loss prevention, confidential-computing, logging, and authorization systems rather than replace them. Those mechanisms continue to protect identities, stores, channels, and individual permissions. The additional problem addressed here is governance of the relationship created between authorized fragments and governance of the transition from computed meaning to actual consequence . The paper presents this as a forward-looking threat model rather than an allegation concerning any specific enterprise or AI product. The objective is to identify an architectural risk
items.title: Enterprise AI as a Reconstruction Layer: Governing Derived Knowledge and Execution-Time Consequences

items.summary: This repository contains the data, documentation, and replication materials associated with the data paper on the  Cartulario de Santo Toribio de Liébana . The dataset provides a structured reconstruction of the documentary collection edited by Luis Sánchez Belda and converts the information contained in the cartulary into machine-readable research data. It covers 566 documentary acts and includes linked information on 576 payment or counter-performance elements, 603 place names, and 1,348 identified persons , together with a concordance between documentary numbering systems. The package preserves the documentary structure of the source while providing standardized variables suitable for quantitative and computational historical research. Particular attention is given to economic transactions. Payments and other forms of material counter-performance are recorded at the individual-component level rather than collapsed into a single transaction value. The data also distinguish operative contractual provisions from penalty clauses and other formulaic diplomatic material. Contains the materials required to reproduce and audit the construction of the dataset, including the structured datasets, extraction and coding documentation, variable definitions, provenance information, validation materials, and the code used for data processing and quality-control procedures. The replication workflow documents the transformation from the published documentary source to the final structured tables. It records corrections and normalization decisions while maintaining traceability to the underlying documentary act. The package is therefore intended not only to reproduce the published dataset but also to make individual coding decisions auditable. The dataset is designed for reuse in research on medieval economic history, property transactions, monastic institutions, historical geography, social networks, and computational approaches to diplomatic sources.
items.title: Replication package for the Santo Toribio de Liébana medieval cartulary dataset

items.summary: Benchmark package accompanying the manuscript “Failure boundary of physics-informed neural networks for moving singular-source problems: residual-error decoupling, an attainable-accuracy bound and an identifiability benchmark”. The package contains: the exact solution of the beam–two-mass moving-load benchmark and the modal and RK4 reference baselines on the same grid; the training campaign with random seeds, network configurations, collocation densities, training budgets, measured wall-clock times, residuals and relative-L2 errors for every run; the inverse-problem (speed and load-amplitude) campaign with its identifiability verdict; the weights of the reference physics-informed network; and the scripts that regenerate every figure, table and number of the paper. It supports two results of the paper: the residual–error decoupling for moving singular sources, and the attainable-accuracy bound obtained by fitting the same architecture to the exact solution. All runs are seeded, so the accuracy–cost comparison reported in the paper can be re-derived without retraining.

items.summary: This record contains the complete R and Python code and supporting documentation for the independent sensitivity reanalysis associated with the manuscript “Swab-based stool collection largely preserves gut microbiome structure with small device-dependent effects: an intra-individual evaluation of sampling devices and processing conditions.” The archive includes scripts to reconstruct and validate anonymous sample metadata from the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) run report and FASTQ filenames; perform preliminary read-quality and paired-read overlap assessments; process forward (R1) and reverse (R2) reads separately using DADA2; infer ASVs; assign taxonomy using the SILVA SSU NR99 release 138.2 training set; construct phylogenetic trees; evaluate sequencing-depth dependence; calculate standardized alpha- and beta-diversity metrics, including Faith’s phylogenetic diversity, weighted UniFrac, and Bray–Curtis dissimilarity; compare the R1 and R2 results; assess sensitivity to rarefaction depth and unusually long terminal branches; and generate the corresponding tables and figures. The archive also contains a complete execution guide, software dependencies and versions, random seeds, original R session information, reference-database details, and file-integrity checksums. Sample metadata and analytical outputs are generated locally by the documented workflow and are not distributed as precomputed files. Raw paired-end sequencing data are publicly available from the European Nucleotide Archive under accession PRJEB107991. The DADA2-formatted SILVA 138.2 taxonomic training set is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14169026 . The independent ASV analyses complement, but do not reproduce or replace, the proprietary MicrobAT® workflow used for the primary OTU-based analysis. MicrobAT® algorithms, OTU-assignment parameters, and the release of its embedded reference database were not disclosed by the software provider. Accordingly, this archive supports reproducibility of the independent R1/R2 ASV sensitivity analyses and downstream analyses of the published MicrobAT® outputs, but not reconstruction of the proprietary MicrobAT®-generated OTU and taxonomic profiles. This version supersedes the earlier R-only archive by adding the Python utilities, complete operational documentation, software-environment records, random seeds, integrity checks, and portable figure-generation scripts.
items.title: Reproducibility code for: Swab-based stool collection largely preserves gut microbiome structure with small device-dependent effects

items.summary: Background. Frailty is often raised as a reason to withhold complete revascularization from older patients after myocardial infarction, although the FIRE trial found no interaction between frailty and the benefit of physiology-guided complete revascularization. Objective. To estimate the cost-effectiveness of physiology-guided complete versus culprit-lesion-only revascularization after successful culprit-lesion percutaneous coronary intervention in patients aged 75 years or older with myocardial infarction and multivessel disease, overall and across Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) strata, from the German statutory health insurance perspective. Methods. A three-year cohort model with quarterly cycles was anchored to the FIRE marginal outcomes (primary composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke or ischaemia-driven revascularization 22.9% versus 29.8%; cardiovascular death or myocardial infarction 12.8% versus 18.2%; heart-failure hospitalisation 14.3% versus 19.7%). Risks in CFS 1-3, 4 and 5-9 were obtained by external calibration that preserved these trial marginals, with a relative treatment effect common to all strata. Costs used 2026 German diagnosis-related-group tariffs. Every input was classified by provenance, and uncertainty was assessed with 20,000 probabilistic draws, one-way and scenario analyses, and break-even analysis. Results. Complete revascularization cost EUR 757 more per patient and yielded 0.056 additional quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of EUR 13,601 per QALY. Ratios were EUR 20,541 per QALY in CFS 1-3, EUR 8,640 in CFS 4 and EUR 8,662 in CFS 5-9. The probability of cost-effectiveness at EUR 30,000 per QALY was 92.5% overall and 78.6%, 96.5% and 97.7% across strata. At that value, the minimum three-year absolute reduction in the primary composite required for cost-effectiveness was 4.3 per 100 patients overall, against a modelled trial effect of 6.9. Staging the additional procedure as a separate admission was the most influential cost driver. Conclusions. Within three years, physiology-guided complete revascularization appears cost-effective at reference values of EUR 20,000 to EUR 50,000 per QALY, and estimated cost-effectiveness was not attenuated in the frailer strata. The stratum-specific estimates rest on external frailty calibration rather than on frailty-specific FIRE outcomes and are not evidence of effect modification.
items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Physiology-Guided Complete Revascularization Across Frailty Strata in Older Patients with Myocardial Infarction: A German Analysis Informed by the FIRE Trial

items.summary: This paper refines the finiteness conjecture for stability architectures and establishes the strongest currently provable results. A stability claim is treated as a profile specifying the object, state space, evolution, perturbation class, projection, failure region, time horizon, and obstructing gap or invariant. An architecture abstracts the structural core: the category of state spaces, the operator class, the gap functional, and the transport obstruction. The paper proves that stability cannot be classified from the trajectory map alone; the full profile matters. For linear systems, there are exactly three distinct architectures: dissipative, geometric or gradient, and Hamiltonian. For model-theoretic stability, the classification is finite and known: stability, NIP, simplicity, and rosiness. This logical classification is an analogy, not a direct translation to dynamics. For Hamiltonian systems, conditional finiteness identifies five candidate mechanisms: KAM persistence, Nekhoroshev confinement, Trojan resonance-gap suppression, symmetry constraint, and barrier obstruction. For statistical systems, four candidates appear: uniform, partial, and non-uniform hyperbolicity, plus rate conditions. In both cases, finiteness follows only if the lists are exhaustive, which remains conjectural. The paper also proves an intra-architecture transfer theorem, a qualified cross-architecture rigidity theorem, and a proposition on overlapping architectures. Transfer works within a shared architecture because estimates depend only on structural data. Rigidity blocks transfer between structurally distinct architectures unless additional structure exists. Overlap is possible, allowing multiple stability mechanisms and multiple failure routes. The general classification problem is undecidable, proved by reduction from the halting problem. Limitations include autonomous, finite-dimensional, smooth dynamics; time-dependent, infinite-dimensional, non-smooth, and nonlinear cases remain open. The consequences concern analog laboratories, engineering design by architecture selection, and a finite core of stability theory. The central message is that the finiteness conjecture is not vacuous: it holds where testable, while full generality awaits resolution of the exhaustiveness conjectures.
items.title: Stability Architectures: A Finite Classification of Provable Cases

items.summary: Our earlier note (rejected from an SC26 AI4S workshop, subsequently published as AIIT Bulletin Vol. 20) compared classical reduced-order models (POD, DMD) against naive neural surrogates (a fully-connected network, a CNN) on textbook-scale problems (lid-driven cavity, dam-break), on a single consumer GPU workstation. That note left five concrete gaps: no graph-based neural baseline, no industrially complex geometry, weak statistical evidence (nine snapshots, a single seed), no learned-dynamics counterpart to DMD, and no hyperparameter search for the neural baselines. This paper closes four of those five. The test case is an industrially representative two-phase stirred tank — a six-blade rotating impeller on a sliding (AMI) mesh, a bottom sparger injecting gas into water, ∼167k cells, solved with OpenFOAM's twoPhaseEulerFoam — run entirely on a single Mac Studio (Apple M4 Max, 14 cores, no discrete GPU). We benchmark five methods (POD, DMD, a neural network, a Graph Neural Operator, and a Deep Koopman autoencoder) on a genuine extrapolation task, backed by a 400-run statistical-robustness sweep, hyperparameter searches for both neural baselines, a check across three impeller speeds, and a four-level forcing-irregularity sweep (quasi-periodic through chaotic, direction-reversing impeller motion) intended to locate DMD's failure point. DMD wins consistently across every data scale, truncation choice, operating condition, and forcing-irregularity level tested, at both a 1 s and an extended 3 s prediction horizon – we did not find the failure threshold we went looking for, and report that directly. The search was not wasted, however: a Deep Koopman autoencoder, competitive at 1 s, degrades sharply at 3 s from compounding autoregressive rollout error (exposure bias); two independent, cheap mitigations – a physical [0, 1] clip mirroring the Graph Neural Operator's own implicit stabilization, and multi-step scheduled-sampling training – each recover roughly a third to a half of the gap without closing it, confirming the diagnosis. A separate, unplanned check turns up a sharper result: ranking methods by mass conservation rather than per-cell accuracy reorders them completely, with the most accurate method (DMD) only third-best at holding a basic physical invariant. We treat all three investigations as concrete instances of a broader, practical question for this community: how much genuine, open-ended scientific investigation — not just a fixed benchmark — can a single high-end workstation support before an HPC allocation is actually necessary? All code, case files, and Colab notebooks are released on GitHub for reproduction.
items.title: How Far Does One Workstation Go? A Pre-HPC Efficiency Check for Industrial-Scale CFD and Reduced-Order Model Benchmarking

items.summary: Anticoncentration is a key ingredient in complexity theoretic arguments for quantum advantage from Gaussian boson sampling. Here we prove polynomial small ball anticoncentration for complex Gaussian transpose Gram hafnians and complex symmetric Gaussian hafnians. For a k × 2n matrix X with independent standard complex Gaussian entries, we establish polynomial small ball anticoncentration for haf(XᵀX) under k ≥ 4n and n²/k = O(log n). For hafnians of 2n × 2n complex symmetric Gaussian matrices, polynomial small ball anticoncentration holds for every n ≥ 1. In both ensembles, any prescribed inverse polynomial failure probability can be achieved with an inverse polynomial small ball radius, uniformly over all centers. These results go beyond moment based anticoncentration by controlling the probability of small hafnian amplitudes. The proof combines Fourier compression with conditional Wishart geometry to handle dependent hafnian cofactors. items.summary: This technical note investigates whether operator-relative noncentrality can predict the relative empirical power of complementary localized scan statistics in correlated spectra. The motivating real-data benchmark compares BABAR and BESIII measurements of the e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻ cross section in the ρ-resonance region on a common 5 MeV grid from 0.600 to 0.880 GeV. The real-data comparison remains negative, with no statistically supported localized shape tension identified. The methodological study compares a coherent-yield scan with a covariance-profiled shape scan and defines the frozen coordinate Θ = log(ES/EY), where ES and EY represent maximum local operator-accessible signal strengths. An archival confirmatory replication used 50,000 null calibration draws per covariance environment, 15,000 independent null-validation draws per environment, 1,440 signal/covariance conditions, and 576,000 injected pseudoexperiments. Θ predicted which scan had greater empirical power with pooled AUC 0.9820 and mean leave-one-covariance-environment-out AUC 0.9740; its correlation with the empirical power difference was 0.9185. Independent Type-I error estimates ranged from 0.0466 to 0.0540. The results support operator-relative noncentrality as a useful empirical coordinate for complementary globally calibrated scans within the tested benchmark. The underlying ingredients, including Gaussian noncentrality, covariance-weighted subspace detection, quadratic scanning, and Monte Carlo calibration, are established; the contribution is a reproducible computational synthesis and controlled characterization rather than a claim of a new general statistical law

The package preserves the documentary structure of the source while providing standardized variables suitable for quantitative and computational historical research. Particular attention is given to economic transactions. Payments and other forms of material counter-performance are recorded at the individual-component level rather than collapsed into a single transaction value. The data also distinguish operative contractual provisions from penalty clauses and other formulaic diplomatic material. Contains the materials required to reproduce and audit the construction of the dataset, including the structured datasets, extraction and coding documentation, variable definitions, provenance information, validation materials, and the code used for data processing and quality-control procedures. The replication workflow documents the transformation from the published documentary source to the final structured tables. It records corrections and normalization decisions while maintaining traceability to the underlying documentary act. The package is therefore intended not only to reproduce the published dataset but also to make individual coding decisions auditable. The dataset is designed for reuse in research on medieval economic history, property transactions, monastic institutions, historical geography, social networks, and computational approaches to diplomatic sources.

Pre-registered study: 500 English prose-refinement tasks across ten domains, two generator models (Gemma4 12B-IT-QAT and 26B-A4B-IT-QAT), 8,000 generations, 999 blind position-swapped pairwise judgments. The governor cuts refinement tokens by 36.6% / 33.1% (bootstrap 95% CIs 33.6-39.5% / 30.3-35.9%) versus an always-eight-iterations baseline — 2.2-3.4x a naive convergence stop — at a measured quality cost reported at equal prominence: 38.0% / 36.6% of judged comparisons lost overall, a majority among actual interventions (61.1% / 59.0%), with measured cost almost perfectly collinear with output length. A full-data ablation shows the saturation signal is simultaneously the savings engine and the dominant cost source, yielding a measured two-point dial (10.0-11.5% savings at 8.2-11.8% loss rate with saturation disabled). ABSTRACT & EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The **Universal Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) Framework** is a formal, production-grade Python architecture designed to enable autonomous, safe, and verifiable self-optimization in computational entities. Grounded in rigor meeting NASA fault-tolerance standards and Google high-performance software engineering specifications, the framework formalizes the OODA (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act) operational loop for arbitrary executable targets—spanning algorithmic functions, machine learning pipelines, and abstract syntax tree (AST) source code.
